extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians, comedy writers, and performers learning observational comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for creating observational stand-up material: techniques to find comedic observations and a short rubric for judging whether an observation will land with an audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watching the Gap
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch the gap between what people say they want and what they actually do. The disconnect = comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek behavior/words mismatches in everyday life; the comedic value comes from exposing that disconnect. Use real examples of intention vs action to build material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the Invisible Visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows you what you see every day but never question; pays attention to nuances; common prompts: 'Did you ever notice…?' / 'What's the deal with…?'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for overlooked, mundane details and articulate them clearly. Framing the observation as a spotlight on something familiar but unspoken increases relatability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tiny Problems Are Windows
rubrics_metrics.description: Tiny problems are windows into bigger truths; small annoyances signal friction, inefficiency, unmet needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a small, specific annoyance as an entry point to reveal larger social or human truths. Treat micro-observations as evidence for a broader comedic claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression and Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: "The closer you can get the jokes together, the bigger the laughs." Aim to trigger 'the roll'—laughter building on itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tighten transitions and reduce filler between jokes to maintain momentum. Arrange bits to accelerate rhythm and create cumulative payoff; edit ruthlessly for pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke Anatomy in Observational Comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Setup builds expectation around the observation; punchline relieves the tension. Anatomy applied to mundane subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft setups that clearly establish the familiar context and then deliver a punchline that reframes or resolves the tension. Ensure the setup is specific enough to make the surprise land.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition (does the audience say 'I've thought that too!')
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recognition": the audience feels 'I've thought that too!' — a key mechanism that makes observational comedy work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure success by whether listeners mentally or audibly agree. Choose topics with broad experiential overlap for the intended audience so recognition is likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity (avoid vague observations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specificity: vague observations don't land — specific ones do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete details, precise images, and exact phrasing over broad generalities. Specifics create stronger recognition and make punchlines more quotable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth (rooted in actual everyday experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth: observational material should be rooted in actual everyday experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground jokes in believable, lived moments; authenticity increases audience buy-in. Avoid fabrications that undermine the feeling of shared reality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise (fresh angle on the familiar)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprise: deliver a fresh angle on the familiar to make the observation funny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine recognition with an unexpected twist or reframe. The punchline should transform the ordinary observation by revealing an unseen implication or absurdity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the topic something the audience knows but rarely articulates?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the topic something the audience knows but rarely articulates?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the subject is a commonplace experience that people won't typically vocalize; those are prime observational targets because verbalizing them creates the comedic moment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the observation specific (not generic)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for concrete details and precise language. Replace vague statements with vivid examples to increase impact and memorability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the audience experience recognition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess audience response: do listeners identify with the observation immediately? Recognition is a key signal that the material will resonate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a surprising angle on the familiar?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a surprising angle on the familiar?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm the punchline reframes the setup in an unexpected way. Surprise differentiates an observation from a mere truism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the language tight enough to be quoted?
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the language tight enough to be quoted?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for concise, memorable phrasing—edit to remove excess words. Quotable lines increase shareability and longevity of the bit.
